hero.eyebrow: Lake Tahoe homeowners, architects, and builders
hero.h1: Lighting Control Installation in Lake Tahoe
hero.sub: Every light in the home set from a keypad, the app, or your voice, with scenes, schedules, and the color of the light tuned to the hour. Designed, installed, and serviced by one team since 1998.

items.p: One button sets the whole room: scenes for morning, dinner, a movie, and bedtime.
Every light in the house from the app or your voice, at home or from the road.
Bright white light by day, warm light at night. The color of the light changes with the hour, not just how bright it is.

about.h2: Lake Tahoe and Las Vegas since 1998
about.p: Since 1998, Holm Electric has partnered with homeowners and contractors on residential electrical, home automation, and integration work. Our engineers design the system to fit how you live now and later, and you get a fully documented project when it is done.

photos.alt: Vanity lights on both sides of a mirror in a wood-clad bathroom
Wall sconces in a home theater with leather seating
A built-in media wall under ceiling spots

steps.p: We meet with you and the owner, walk the plans, and settle how every space will be lit and controlled.
Our engineers design the system to the plans: fixtures, loads, keypad locations, and the wiring your crew pulls once.
We install, program, and test every scene before the owner moves in, and tune it once they do.
You get a fully documented project with drawings, so service and upgrades never depend on one installer's memory.

items.p: We’re in a very old cabin in KB that’s going through probate and has a lot of issues. After having an emergency electric shut off, I was told by Liberty Utilities I needed a full panel replacement and inspection before returning power.
Very helpful and professional. Pricing estimates very high as is everything else. Will not do project because of high costs.
I had a very small job that required replacing a low voltage transformer and replacing some LED strips. It DID take a while to get their attention but once I did they did the job.

services.h2: More we do for the home

items.p: Music in every room, from one app.
Projector, screen, surround sound, and seating.
Shades that move with the light and the scenes.

final.p: Tell us about the home and we will set a time.

footer.creds: Holm Electric, Inc. Since 1998. Systems we integrate: Lutron, Ketra, Savant, RTI. Las Vegas office: 5045 S Rogers St, Ste. 3, Las Vegas, NV 89118, 702-818-3781.

notes: Built 2026-10-06 from Jonathan's Loom audit of holmelectric.com/residential/ (one page for all residential services, with an interactive map in the hero). The map is left off on purpose: he said it is likely hurting conversion. The headline names Lake Tahoe because their first office is Incline Village and the residential page lists Lake Tahoe first; Las Vegas is in the footer. Their site's blue is #799EC8 (white on it reads at 2.79:1), so the button and card blue is the same hue one step darker, #4A78B0 (4.56:1); #799EC8 is the accent on the process step rules. Poppins is the face their site uses; the serif titles come from the engine (high-end residential rule). The hero photo is their own bar-with-pendants interior from the home page, served at 959 px wide, so it is soft on a wide screen; the sharper lakefront home at dusk (1920 px) sits behind the process band and would be the swap if he wants the hero sharper. No reviews, rating, team photo, license number, or awards are on their site: the review boxes and the about photo are marked empty, there is no trust line, and the footer carries only what the site states. The three secondary service cards all link to /residential/ because no page per service exists yet (his first point in the Loom). The form sends nothing.
